properties.title: Surg-UniWorld: A Unified Surgical World Model with Multimodal Control Experts
properties.identity_boundary: Read from supplied title-page text and upstream image-review notes; not independently retrieved.

properties.review_access: Complete page-indexed text and prior automated image-review notes. This synthesis call did not receive page images directly.
properties.supplements: No separately supplied supplement; no appendix identified in the ten-page document.

properties.design: Offline conditional surgical-video generation benchmark, modality-subset experiments, and architecture/training ablations.
properties.data: Actual recorded laparoscopic video from Cholec80, with estimated and manually curated annotations.
properties.clinical_boundary: Visual-generation results do not establish actual-care decisions, operative success, or patient benefit.

properties.name: Surg-UniWorld
properties.backbone: Pretrained Wan2.2 video diffusion backbone; added controls trained with latent flow matching.
properties.configuration: Full optional-control configuration unless another subset or ablation is explicitly identified.
properties.membership_status: Primary-source core-WM identity unresolved. Legacy core membership retained as provisional, not verified.
properties.membership_reason: Learned conditional successor-video generation is implemented, but persistent appearance-reference memory is not sufficiently established as an evolving health-world state advanced between prediction/update operations.
properties.identity_guard: Recursive generation is not universally required. The unresolved issue is state advancement over the procedural coordinate, not the mere use of block generation or a frozen backbone.
properties.capability_boundary: Later-frame conditional synthesis is evaluated. A qualifying evolving-state implementation and evaluated dependence on a specified action are not jointly established sufficiently for an ontology L2 demonstration.

properties.flow: First-frame appearance and temporal masks → regional anchor memories and shape features; optional edge/depth/flow → separate encoding and anchor-relative experts; additive stage-wise composition → Wan2.2 hints → generated video.
properties.planner: No model-coupled procedural action optimizer or policy in the documented evaluated pipeline.
properties.profile_reason: BP_COMPONENT represents the evaluated conditional generator/resource contribution while strict core-WM identity remains unresolved.
properties.deployment_boundary: Offline research inference, not demonstrated clinical deployment.

properties.purpose: Research on condition-guided generation of laparoscopic instrument–tissue interaction video.
properties.required_context: Reference frame, video-level description, and complete temporal hierarchical masks.
properties.optional_context: Temporally aligned edge, depth, and optical-flow sequences.
properties.application_boundary: Downstream applications are motivations or implications, not demonstrated utility endpoints.
properties.authority: No documented clinical or physical action-execution authority.

properties.name: Cholec80-SurgWAM
properties.version_boundary: Dataset described in the read manuscript; no independently pinned derivative release.
properties.selection: Pronounced instrument motion and limited background motion.
properties.annotation: SAM2 initialization with manual mask refinement; unspecified VLM descriptions; Depth Anything 3, WAFT, and HED estimated controls.
properties.access_boundary: Parent resource described as public; derivative asset availability and license not established.

properties.count_unit_boundary: Clips, frames, and masks are not unique-patient counts.

properties.independence_limits: Patient/site identities, clip-overlap audit, and the role of video61–70 are not reported.
properties.metric_denominator_boundary: The test-set size is stated; exact generated sample counts entering each metric are not explicitly stated.

properties.feedback_mode: Block generation with complete temporal masks and optional temporal visual controls; not recursive feedback.
properties.reference: Recorded test video and estimator-derived controls.
properties.comparability_limit: Each baseline receives conditions supported by its own interface; comparisons are not uniformly input-matched.
properties.first_frame_in_evaluation: Not reported; first-frame exclusion is explicit only for training loss.
properties.uncertainty_and_tolerances: No reported confidence intervals, repeated-seed dispersion, or acceptance tolerances.

properties.configuration: Full controls plus always-on first-frame/text/mask inputs.
properties.environment: Offline inference compared with retrospective human surgical recordings.
properties.endpoint: Conditional visual fidelity, realism, and control adherence.

properties.configurations: Eight optional-modality subsets, training losses, subset sampling, region grounding/scaling, architecture, and composition strategies.
properties.comparison_boundary: Visual-condition and design comparisons, not matched alternative surgical action regimes.
properties.result_boundary: Quality/adherence trade-offs; the proposed configuration does not dominate every individual metric.

properties.responsibility: Appearance/mask encoding and typed optional-condition encoding/fusion.
properties.contract_boundary: No full units, information-release, or missing-required-input contract established.

properties.responsibility: Regional first-frame appearance reference and shape-conditioned anchor construction.
properties.state_boundary: Reference memory is implemented; an evolved current-state or posterior filtering service is not established.

properties.responsibility: Conditional latent video generation and observable video emission.
properties.time_boundary: Video index is separate from denoising, network depth, and optimization iterations.
properties.transition_boundary: A recursively advanced scene state is not established; recurrence is not imposed as a universal membership condition.

properties.responsibility: VLM-generated instrument–tissue interaction descriptions during dataset construction.
properties.scope_boundary: Offline annotation component; not an inference-time decision agent.

properties.representation: Video-level text specifying intended surgical action.
properties.grounding_boundary: No calibrated robot-command or validated clinical operation mapping.
properties.evaluation_boundary: The pipeline consumes descriptions, but action-dependent predictive behavior is not isolated by the reported control-subset experiments.

properties.evaluated_extent: 49 frames including supplied I0; remaining T−1 frames synthesized.
properties.non_entailment: None of these algorithmic counts establishes elapsed clinical time or a supported forecast horizon.

Surg-UniWorld: A Unified Surgical World Model
with Multimodal Control Experts

Rulin Zhou, Wanhao Liu, Guoheng Ma, Liangjin Shao, Qiujie Song, Yidu Wang, Guankun Wang, Tong
Chen, Long Bai, Luping Zhou, and Hongliang Ren,

Code and video demonstrations
are available athttps://surg-uniworld.pages.dev/.

generating targeted roll-
outs for robotic policy learning, and simulating dynamic endo-
scopic environments for surgical training.

a textual instruction spec-
ifies the intended surgical action, while the first frame and
hierarchical semantic masks provide persistent observations of
scene appearance and spatial organization.

We construct Cholec80-SurgW AM from the public
Cholec80 dataset following the pipeline in Fig. 2. Instruments
are first localized, and W AFT optical flow is used to
select clips with pronounced instrument motion and limited
background motion, reducing the influence of global camera
movement [19]. SAM2 then provides initial masks, which are
manually reviewed and refined into hierarchical annotations
of instruments, target tissues, and background tissues [20].
A vision–language model generates descriptions of the
corresponding instrument–tissue interactions. Aligned depth,
optical-flow, and edge controls are obtained using Depth
Anything 3, W AFT, and HED, respectively [19], [21], [22].

Here,I 0 is the given
reference frame, which provides the initial visual context for
subsequent generation. It is preserved throughout the denoising
process, while the model synthesizes the remainingT−1
frames. The corresponding video-level surgical description is
denoted byY.

WhenU S =∅, generation is conditioned only on the text,
reference appearance, and hierarchical semantic structure. Oth-
erwise, one or more modalities further constrain the boundary,
geometry, and motion of the generated surgical video.

In implementation, the reference frame is temporally
repeated to match the video-conditioning interface, while only
the first temporal token plane is retained to constructP 0.
Therefore,P 0 is derived exclusively from the observed frame
and provides a shared appearance reference for all control
stages.

Here,D i(·)aligns the semantic masks with the token resolu-
tion of thei-th control stage,B(·)extracts region boundaries,
and∆ τ denotes temporal mask differences. We useτfor video
time to distinguish it from the diffusion timestep. The region
weightsW i identify the locations of the instrument, foreground
tissue, and background tissue, whereas the shape tokensS i
encode their contours and temporal structural evolution.

The masked attention uses the
corresponding region weights as spatial biases and employs
multiple learnable queries for each region. This allows the re-
sulting memory to preserve diverse local appearance patterns,
including instrument reflections, heterogeneous tissue textures,
and spatially varying illumination. WhenW i is applied toP 0,
only its first temporal plane, aligned with the appearance-token
resolution, is used.

The experts share the same architecture
but have independent parameters. Each expert is reused across
all eight control stages and interprets its modality relative
to the same surgical anchor rather than redefining the scene
independently.
Each available control sequenceU m is first converted into
a V ACE-compatible latent using its validity maskΩ m.

All modalities share the
V ACE encoder parameters but use separate forward passes,
without token concatenation or cross-modal attention. Miss-
ing modalities are skipped. The shared encoder provides a
common feature space, while the typed stems and modality
embeddings preserve modality identity.

The availability indicatora m =I[m∈S]
is determined directly from the input; unavailable modalities
are skipped during V ACE encoding and expert inference.
Each expert increment is scaled by a learnable stage-wise
factorλ m,i =σ(s m,i)∈(0,1), which captures the varying
importance of modalitymacross the control hierarchy without
input-dependent prediction or cross-modal normalization.

5) Overall objectiveL:To reduce the computational cost of
counterfactual inference, we evaluate the control benefit and
marginal consistency losses everyK= 16optimization steps.
Letχ k =I[kmodK= 0], wherekis the current optimization
step. The complete training objective is
L=L FM +λ TSLTS +χ k (λCBLCB +λ MCLMC).(21)
We setλ TS = 0.1andλ CB =λ MC = 0.01in all experiments.
Here,Sdenotes the set of available optional controls, exclud-
ing the always-on surgical anchor. For anchor-only samples
(S=∅), onlyL FM andL TS are applied. The control benefit
lossL CB is activated when|S| ≥1, while the marginal
consistency lossL MC is additionally activated when|S| ≥2.

2) Temporal Structure LossL TS:AlthoughL FM improves
reconstruction in important regions, it does not explicitly con-
strain inter-frame variations. To suppress instrument flickering,
contour discontinuities, and inconsistent tissue motion, we
match the temporal velocity differences:

1) Dataset and Baselines:All experiments are conducted
on Cholec80-SurgW AM using 49-frame clips at a resolution
of832×480. We consider two evaluation settings: sur-
gical video prediction from text and the first frame, cov-
ering LTXV-2B [12], Wan2.2-5B [13], Cosmos-H-Predict-
2B [4], SurgSora [8], and Endora [7]; and controllable gen-
eration with additional spatial or motion conditions, cov-
ering Cosmos-H-Transfer-2B [4], V ACE-Wan2.2 [15], and
ControlNet-Wan2.2 [14]. Each baseline is evaluated with the
conditions supported by its interface, whereas Surg-UniWorld
uses first-frame appearance and hierarchical masks as the
surgical anchor and supports arbitrary subsets of optional
depth, edge, and optical-flow controls.

2) Evaluation Metrics:Following the unified video-
generation evaluation protocol adopted in V ACE [15], we
evaluate the surgical videos generated using PSNR, SSIM,
LPIPS, FID and FVD. PSNR and SSIM measure pixel-level
fidelity and structural similarity, whereas LPIPS evaluates
perceptual similarity. FID measures frame-level distribution
quality, while FVD captures spatiotemporal realism. Higher
PSNR and SSIM and lower LPIPS, FID, and FVD indicate
better performance. To evaluate control adherence, we
also report Edge F1, Depth si-RMSE, and Flow EPE for
configurations containing the corresponding control modality.
Following prior controllable generation protocols [23], each
condition is re-extracted from the generated video using
a fixed modality estimator and compared with the input
control.

3) Implementation Details:For all modality-conditioned
methods, the pretrained generative backbone is frozen and only
the additional control modules are optimized for 7,500 steps on
four NVIDIA H100 GPUs using AdamW with a learning rate
of2×10 −5. The number of control injection layers is fixed to
N= 8for Surg-UniWorld, V ACE-Wan2.2, and ControlNet-
Wan2.2.

These results support separating persistent
